newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia wool indicator rise 5.0 cents to 678c/kg.
newsitem.headline: Australia wool indicator rise 5.0 cents to 678c/kg.

text.p: The Australian wool market eastern indicator rose five cents to 678 cents a kg clean on Thursday at sales in Sydney, Wool International said.
Merino fleece was dearer, with 19/20/21/23/25 microns up to one percent dearer, 22/24m 0.5 percent dearer, and 26m 1.5 percent dearer.
Merino skirtings of 19 to 21m were generally unchanged.
Crossbreds were dearer, with 27-30m up two percent and 31m up one percent.
In cardings, washing locks were unchanged, light carbonising locks slightly cheaper, and crutchings generally unchanged.
WI said Japanese interests were principal buyers with most sectors of the trade active.
Of the 12,954 bales offered, 6.9 percent were passed in.
In early Fremantle selling, merino fleece ranged from generally unchanged for 23/24m to one percent dearer for 21m and 25m and 1.5 percent dearer for 22m.
In cardings, locks were fully firm.
The early pass-in rate was five percent. The scheduled Fremantle offering was 17,132 bales.
Sales continue next week in Sydney and Melbourne with about 72,200 bales to be offered.
